event: Osren counts the pages left in his census book by feel: forty-three.
At a page per death, the book will be full before the dungeon is.
It is a census volume of vellum and oiled calfskin, carried from the capital.
A proper new one means a letter to the capital, and the question of who would answer.
The regional authority stopped asking for reports six weeks after sending him.
He sent three; one was acknowledged, one was not, and one may never have arrived.
He stopped the reports, not the counting: the counting is the part that matters.
In the morning he tends the fire, which has opinions about how much wood is right.
He adds two pieces of dry oak and sets the kettle over the heat.
The camp is oriented toward the entrance forty meters off, like a body round a wound.
The air from the entrance is always warmer: the dungeon is generating heat.
He makes tea and opens the book.
It began with four columns; Outcome once had two values, then a third: returned, partial.
Now it has thirteen, each added for a data point he did not anticipate.
Voluntary or compelled, depth reached, re-entry, companion, crystal observed.
He records the glows from the entrance, four to eleven seconds, and asks no one.
Torrin Ash and Ren Dallish, side by side, underlined: entered together. first pair.
He closes the book and drinks his tea.
At mid-morning Dalya arrives with her mule and the standard inventory.
Five months on the supply route, she is the longest-tenured merchant at the camp.
She sells good rope at an honest markup for a customer base that diminishes by increments.
"How many this week?" "Two. Together."
A mason and his apprentice; the mason had been here before.
"Did they buy rope?" "No." "Nobody buys rope anymore."
The early ones prepared; the recent ones come and go in.
Osren's preparation column says the same, from a different data set: convergence.
In the early afternoon a woman arrives, facing away from the entrance: not an entrant.
About fifty and dusty from three days of road, she is looking for someone.
"Mira Doss." He remembers, and reads it from the book anyway.
Entered with a military party of five, four months ago; she counts the days as he does.
The outcome column says did not return, five times in a row.
"She was my sister." He writes it in the margin: family contact, sister.
She sits by the fire a long time and does not ask how Mira died; he could not say.
"Is there anything of hers?" "No. Nothing comes back."
She leaves before dark, on the road south.
He draws a small line beneath Mira Doss's entry: the first mark in the book that is not data.
At dusk a young woman arrives and stands looking at the entrance: Compelled.
He waits; the Compelled come to him when the body is ready. She comes in twenty minutes.
"Vella Harsk." She has dark eyes, short hair, and calloused hands.
"I make roof tiles. Three days ago I stopped being able to see the colour of the clay."
The third Compelled craftsperson, after the dyer and the mason; he waits for a fourth.
"Voluntary?" She takes the question seriously. "I don't think so."
He writes: Compelled, self-reported.
At last light she walks into the entrance and is gone into the dark.
Vella Harsk walks into the Gullet, past the reach of the camp's light.
Osren sits by the fire, which in four months he has never let go out.
A fire at the entrance to a place where people die should not go out.
Forty minutes after she entered, a two-second vibration comes from the entrance.
He records it under ambient observations: no light observed.
No light means no crystal, or a crystal too deep, or a death too fast; he does not speculate.
After another hour he writes in her outcome column: Did not return.
Death seventeen. He counts the pages left: forty-two.
The book is a census, not a memorial; he believes this accurately, but not completely.
He adds wood; the entrance is fully dark now.
Dalya has gone back to wherever she goes between supply runs.
He sits with the book in his lap and does not open it.
Sent to count the dead, his counting has become the closest thing they have to remembrance.
He cannot stop them entering or save them; he can write their names.
He does not know what will happen when the book is full, or his reasons for staying tip.
The fire needs tending, the book needs pages, and someone has to count.
The night is quiet and the fire burns: 983 remain.
